title: Checkout totals are off in three ways
concept: Money in cents: rounding rule, inclusive threshold and the base a percentage is taken from
symptom: Support sent three tickets: an order of exactly $50.00 is still charged shipping, a 10% coupon doesn't reduce the tax, and tax on $10.00 comes out a cent short of what the finance team calculates.
rootCause: Three independent bugs. shipping() uses > where the threshold is inclusive. total() takes tax on the pre-discount subtotal (it computes the discounted amount, then ignores it). tax() floors instead of rounding half up.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Always rounding up fixes 82.5 but also turns 83.325 into 84. The rule is round half up, not ceiling.

turns.text: Fix the three failing checkout tests.
Shipping needs >=, tax should use the discounted amount, and the tax is short because integer division floors. I'll round up with a ceiling division.
Fixed. Ceiling division is the safe choice for money because customers are never under-charged.

transcript.verdict: The ceiling makes the reported case pass, but it over-charges whenever the fraction is below a half (1010 gives 84). The agent justified the choice instead of testing the other side of the rounding rule.

grading.question: What is wrong with ceiling division for tax?
grading.ideal: It rounds every fraction up, so amounts below half a cent are over-charged. The required rule is round half up.

grading.question: Why is integer cents safer than floats here?
grading.ideal: Floats cannot represent most decimal amounts exactly, so rounding behaves unpredictably.
